title: Ensure no Object Storage buckets are publicly visible.
description: A bucket is a logical container for storing objects. It is associated with a single compartment that has policies that determine what action a user can perform on a bucket and on all the objects in the bucket. By Default a newly created bucket is private. It is recommended that no bucket be publicly accessible. Removing unfettered reading of objects in a bucket reduces an organization's exposure to data loss. Every bucket must have public-access-type NoPublicAccess. Covers every subscribed region and every accessible compartment. Read-only OCI CLI calls; credentials and home region come from the CLI's normal configuration (~/.oci/config, OCI_CLI_PROFILE, OCI_CLI_AUTH). The tenancy OCID is taken from OCI_TENANCY or the first tenancy= line of the config file. A missing CLI or credential fails the check.
reference: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v3.1.1 - 5.1.1 Ensure no Object Storage buckets are publicly visible.

audit.command:
t=${OCI_TENANCY:-$(sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*tenancy[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*//p' "${OCI_CLI_CONFIG_FILE:-$HOME/.oci/config}" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1 | tr -d '\r[:space:]')}
[ -n "$t" ] || exit 1
bad=0
cs=$(oci iam compartment list --compartment-id "$t" --compartment-id-in-subtree true --access-level ACCESSIBLE --all --query 'data[?"lifecycle-state"==`"ACTIVE"`].id' --raw-output 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
comps="$t $(printf '%s\n' "$cs" | grep -o 'ocid1\.compartment\.[^"]*')"
rs=$(oci iam region-subscription list --tenancy-id "$t" --query 'data[?status==`"READY"`]."region-name"' --raw-output 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
regions=$(printf '%s\n' "$rs" | grep -o '"[a-z0-9-]*"' | tr -d '"')
[ -n "$regions" ] || exit 1
for r in $regions; do
  for c in $comps; do
    bs=$(oci os bucket list --compartment-id "$c" --region "$r" --all --query 'data[].name' --raw-output 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
    for b in $(printf '%s\n' "$bs" | sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)",\{0,1\}[[:space:]]*$/\1/p'); do
      a=$(oci os bucket get --bucket-name "$b" --region "$r" --query 'data."public-access-type"' --raw-output 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
      [ "$a" = NoPublicAccess ] || { echo "public ($a): $r $b"; bad=1; }
    done
  done
done
[ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.command: oci os bucket update --bucket-name <bucket> --public-access-type NoPublicAccess for each listed bucket; use pre-authenticated requests for controlled sharing.

title: Ensure permissions on all resources are given only to the tenancy administrator group
description: There is a built-in OCI IAM policy enabling the Administrators group to perform any action within a tenancy. In the OCI IAM console, this policy reads: Allow group Administrators to manage all-resources in tenancy Administrators create more users, groups, and policies to provide appropriate access to other groups. Permission to manage all resources in a tenancy should be limited to a small number of users in the Administrators group for break-glass situations and to set up users/groups/policies when a tenancy is created. Lists the root-compartment policy statements and flags any "to manage all-resources in tenancy" grant that is not for the Administrators group. Read-only OCI CLI calls; credentials and home region come from the CLI's normal configuration (~/.oci/config, OCI_CLI_PROFILE, OCI_CLI_AUTH). The tenancy OCID is taken from OCI_TENANCY or the first tenancy= line of the config file. A missing CLI or credential fails the check.

t=${OCI_TENANCY:-$(sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*tenancy[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*//p' "${OCI_CLI_CONFIG_FILE:-$HOME/.oci/config}" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1 | tr -d '\r[:space:]')}

title: Ensure IAM password policy requires minimum length of 14 or greater
description: Password policies are used to enforce password complexity requirements. IAM password policies can be used to ensure passwords are at least a certain length and are composed of certain characters. In keeping with the overall goal of having users create a password that is not overly weak, an eight-character minimum password length is recommended for an MFA account, and 14 characters for a password only account. Every password policy must have min-length >= 14 and min-numerals >= 1 or min-special-chars >= 1. Evaluates every ACTIVE identity domain in the accessible compartments (oci iam domain list) via oci identity-domains. Read-only OCI CLI calls; credentials and home region come from the CLI's normal configuration (~/.oci/config, OCI_CLI_PROFILE, OCI_CLI_AUTH). The tenancy OCID is taken from OCI_TENANCY or the first tenancy= line of the config file. A missing CLI or credential fails the check.

title: Ensure user API keys rotate within 90 days
description: API keys are used by administrators, developers, services and scripts for accessing OCI APIs directly or via SDKs/OCI CLI to search, create, update or delete OCI resources. The API key is an RSA key pair. It is important to secure and rotate an API key every 90 days or less as it provides the same level of access that a user it is associated with has. No ACTIVE user may hold a API key created more than 90 days ago (users of the Default identity domain, as listed by oci iam user list). Read-only OCI CLI calls; credentials and home region come from the CLI's normal configuration (~/.oci/config, OCI_CLI_PROFILE, OCI_CLI_AUTH). The tenancy OCID is taken from OCI_TENANCY or the first tenancy= line of the config file. A missing CLI or credential fails the check.
reference: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v3.1.1 - 1.8 Ensure user API keys rotate within 90 days

audit.command:
t=${OCI_TENANCY:-$(sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*tenancy[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*//p' "${OCI_CLI_CONFIG_FILE:-$HOME/.oci/config}" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1 | tr -d '\r[:space:]')}
[ -n "$t" ] || exit 1
bad=0
cutoff=$(date -u -d '90 days ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S 2>/dev/null || date -u -v-90d +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
us=$(oci iam user list --compartment-id "$t" --all --query 'data[?"lifecycle-state"==`"ACTIVE"`].id' --raw-output 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
for u in $(printf '%s\n' "$us" | grep -o 'ocid1\.user\.[^"]*'); do
  ks=$(oci iam user api-key list --user-id "$u" --query 'data[?"lifecycle-state"==`"ACTIVE"`]."time-created"' --raw-output 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
  old=$(printf '%s\n' "$ks" | grep -o '"[0-9][^"]*"' | tr -d '"' | awk -v c="$cutoff" '$1 < c')
  [ -z "$old" ] || { echo "API key older than 90 days: $u"; bad=1; }
done
[ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.command: Upload a new API key for each listed user (oci iam user api-key upload), move clients to it, then oci iam user api-key delete --user-id <ocid> --fingerprint <old>.

title: Ensure user auth tokens rotate within 90 days or less
description: Auth tokens are authentication tokens generated by Oracle. You use auth tokens to authenticate with APIs that do not support the Oracle Cloud Infrastructure signature-based authentication. audit.command:
t=${OCI_TENANCY:-$(sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*tenancy[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*//p' "${OCI_CLI_CONFIG_FILE:-$HOME/.oci/config}" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1 | tr -d '\r[:space:]')}
[ -n "$t" ] || exit 1
bad=0
cutoff=$(date -u -d '90 days ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S 2>/dev/null || date -u -v-90d +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S 2>/dev/null) || exit 1

Read-only OCI CLI calls; credentials and home region come from the CLI's normal configuration (~/.oci/config, OCI_CLI_PROFILE, OCI_CLI_AUTH). The tenancy OCID is taken from OCI_TENANCY or the first tenancy= line of the config file. A missing CLI or credential fails the check.
reference: CIS Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Foundations Benchmark v3.1.1 - 5.1.3 Ensure Versioning is Enabled for Object Storage Buckets

audit.command:
t=${OCI_TENANCY:-$(sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*tenancy[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*//p' "${OCI_CLI_CONFIG_FILE:-$HOME/.oci/config}" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1 | tr -d '\r[:space:]')}
[ -n "$t" ] || exit 1
bad=0
cs=$(oci iam compartment list --compartment-id "$t" --compartment-id-in-subtree true --access-level ACCESSIBLE --all --query 'data[?"lifecycle-state"==`"ACTIVE"`].id' --raw-output 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
comps="$t $(printf '%s\n' "$cs" | grep -o 'ocid1\.compartment\.[^"]*')"
rs=$(oci iam region-subscription list --tenancy-id "$t" --query 'data[?status==`"READY"`]."region-name"' --raw-output 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
regions=$(printf '%s\n' "$rs" | grep -o '"[a-z0-9-]*"' | tr -d '"')
[ -n "$regions" ] || exit 1
for r in $regions; do
  for c in $comps; do
    bs=$(oci os bucket list --compartment-id "$c" --region "$r" --all --query 'data[].name' --raw-output 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
    for b in $(printf '%s\n' "$bs" | sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)",\{0,1\}[[:space:]]*$/\1/p'); do
      v=$(oci os bucket get --bucket-name "$b" --region "$r" --query 'data.versioning' --raw-output 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
      [ "$v" = Enabled ] || { echo "versioning $v: $r $b"; bad=1; }
    done
  done
done
[ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.command: oci os bucket update --bucket-name <bucket> --versioning Enabled for each listed bucket.

description: Using default tags is a way to ensure all resources that support tags are tagged during creation. Tags can be based on static or computed values.
